grh_183a0dbfdb2da8e2c6d9.title: Once Around The Block
paragraphs: An evening walk around one Rivers End block reveals three households whose troubles are quietly connected. Kit McKenzie has just had a baby, but her husband George resents the new expenses because they have consumed the savings he hoped to use to buy the cottage they rent from Pete Williams. Pete, meanwhile, cannot emotionally let go of that cottage because it is tied to an old love and has become a shrine to his past; his wife Jennifer believes she can never compete with the memory and plans to leave him. The last stop is the mansion of elderly recluse Cordelia Bingham, whom the town believes to be a miser. Cordelia reveals that she has secretly given almost her entire fortune to charities around the world and has only $25,000 left, which she asks Dr. Christian to leave to one deserving person in Rivers End. Christian chooses the McKenzies' two-week-old baby. The legacy gives the young family the security to complete the purchase of Pete's cottage, removing the old house from Pete's life and giving Pete and Jennifer a chance to restore their marriage. The single walk around the block thus links a newborn child's future, a troubled marriage and the hidden generosity of a woman everyone had misjudged.

grh_18bbc99236262a4f6ba9.title: The Lone Voyager
paragraphs: When veteran sailor Ian Janis collapses on the eve of a planned round-the-world voyage, his daughter Jessica takes his yacht Adventure to sea and decides to complete the journey for him. She reaches Australia alone, where naval architect David Flynn helps repair the boat while arguing that she is risking her life by continuing. Jessica presses on, learns that her recovering father is proud of her, and survives the most dangerous stages of the voyage, including Cape Horn. When she finally returns home to a waiting fleet, her father and David are there to greet her. Having proved she can make the voyage alone, Jessica realizes she no longer needs to live as though she must do everything alone.

grh_1873c0d5401f601faae0.title: When the Shoe Doesn't Fit
paragraphs: Cindy Lou Ames longs to attend a ranch dance but has nothing suitable to wear, so traveling peddler Friendly DeWitt and Britt transform her with a borrowed dress and a pair of fancy slippers that must be returned by midnight. At the dance, Marty, the boy Cindy has loved for years, is captivated by the elegant stranger but withdraws because he feels he is betraying Cindy. The next morning the borrowed slippers reveal that the mysterious girl and Cindy were the same person. Marty finally admits that he has loved Cindy all along, giving the story its deliberately Cinderella-like ending.

grh_18bcad9da0f6005e553a.title: I Married an Angel
paragraphs: Banker Willie Palaffi marries Brigitta, a literal angel whose complete honesty and innocence make her a disastrous fit for worldly society. Her blunt truthfulness offends people Willie needs for business, and in trying to adapt to earthly life she loses her wings and fears she has become neither angel nor woman. Willie's sister coaches her in social behavior, but Brigitta's honesty ultimately wins over the very duchess whose support the bank needs. Willie tells Brigitta that he loves her as she is, and the pair reconcile without asking her to abandon her angelic nature.

grh_186f49cc08cc41a4d991.title: Pirates of Picadilly
paragraphs: This musical biography follows Gilbert and Sullivan through the brilliant but combative partnership that created their celebrated comic operas. Their clashing personalities repeatedly drive them to work apart, trade insults and insist that each deserves the larger share of credit, yet the quarrels also push both men creatively. At the opening of The Gondoliers they hear an audience singing the songs they have created together and finally confront the absurdity of their estrangement. They admit they may never have liked one another very much, shake hands and immediately begin planning a new work face to face.
